source: Jacques Pelletier: Not Cherokee, not Shawnee, not Tutelo. Perhaps she is from another tribe. Because she is, how you say, a “wretch,” I will trade her for one British Pound.
target: 雅克・佩尔蒂耶：不是切罗基，不是肖尼，也不是图特洛。也许来自别的部落。既然她是，怎么说，「可怜虫」，那一英镑就卖给妳。

source: Gwendolyn Wald: Spare me the fantasies. She bears great need for refinement. Her worth is no more than 10 shillings.
target: 关德琳・沃尔德：省省那些幻想吧。她还需要大量调教，最多值十先令。

source: Gwendolyn Wald: Fine. Fine then, 13 shillings for this wretch.
target: 关德琳・沃尔德：好吧，好吧。这个可怜虫，十三先令。

source: Gwendolyn Wald: She is not some sort of Indian? Loins for clothing and animal-skin shoes...
target: 关德琳・沃尔德：她不是某种印第安人吗？穿腰布、兽皮鞋……

source: Jacques Pelletier: Ah, but she is strong like bison. Quick like fox. A vivante spirit! Two of my men had to rope her. In France, with training, she can be star of Le Cirque de Paris!
target: 雅克・佩尔蒂耶：啊，可她强得像野牛，快得像狐狸。活泼得很！我的两个人才能拿绳子绑住她。到法国，受过训练，她能成为明星，在巴黎马戏团！

source: Jacques Pelletier: Enchanté, Madame Wald. Excuse this child’s, uhh, odd ways, s’il vous plait. She is like animal, scared and fierce with no tongue for language. The bandage on her leg… we found her in the beaver trap meant for a raccoon – a rare creature we spotted with beautiful blanc fur.
target: 雅克・佩尔蒂耶：幸会，沃尔德夫人。这孩子，呃，行为古怪，请您见谅。她像动物，害怕又凶，舌头不会说话。腿上的绷带……我们在捕河狸的夹子里找到她。那本来是要抓浣熊的——我们看见一只稀有的家伙，有着漂亮的白色皮毛。

source: Gwendolyn Wald: Forgive me, monsieur, but she appears of little use to me. Why, we can hardly determine her age.
target: 关德琳・沃尔德：恕我直言，先生，她看来没什么用。连年纪都很难判断。

source: Jacques Pelletier: 13 is fair – she is young and good for… shaping.
target: 雅克・佩尔蒂耶：十三，很公道。她还小，很适合……塑造。

source: Gwendolyn Wald: Ah, good day, Monsieur Pelletier. Please, come in from this cold. Hmm, I see you’ve brought me a true wretch today.
target: 关德琳・沃尔德：啊，日安，佩尔蒂耶先生。外头冷，请进。嗯，看来您今天带了个真正的可怜虫。

source: Gwendolyn Wald: As I live and breathe… the luster, the brilliance. Did you get this green gem around here? This. This. Where?
target: 关德琳・沃尔德：老天爷……这光泽，这光彩。妳在这附近拿到这颗绿宝石的？这个。这个。哪里？

target: 关德琳・沃尔德：瞧见了吧？听话就不挨鞭子。现在，妳这肮脏脖子上挂的是什么……

target: 关德琳・沃尔德：别踢了，妳这魔鬼！妳的手牢牢绑在柱子上，我能在这谷仓里日夜抽妳。山羊可爱看戏了。

target: 关德琳・沃尔德：噢，真受罪！妳彻头彻尾就是个野人。不过，若能带我找到更多祖母绿，蒙上帝允许，过上更体面的日子，教妳说话或许也值得。

source: Feral Child: Rrrrr… (see all my teeth... will fight if I must.)
target: 野孩子：呜——（看我的牙齿……非打不可，我就打。）

source: Don’t stop, run into the woods! Legs be strong… There! WHITE RACCOON! Yes, go, show me! Left by the big pine. Straight now, yes. Familiar rock line, yes. Cold hurts the chest. Body needs food. But I must run back to where I… happened… where I first saw this White Raccoon! After two suns, ugly woman untied my hands and sat down with a bowl of hot mush. Smell was good, like when mother makes deer meat soup with roots. My stomach wanted it. But this ugly woman hurt me. I remembered my hurt, my hunger, and I decided she is trickster. She put two little tools next to bowl. One I recognized as spoon made of something silvery-strange, the other – she pointed down and called it “for-k.” I saw its sharpness. I reached slow for for-k and kept my eyes down. Then I grabbed bowl slow. Splash! Hot mush in her face! And then I speared the for-k sharpness into the side of her head. She howls like the wolf! I tear my gem off her neck and run! Legs are cut from her whipping vine. My hurt foot is hot with pain… Legs be strong… White Raccoon, thank you... There, yes, fallen tree… there, spot where the foot-teeth clamped me… yes… Here! I take string in hand like before, gem swings around my head and, yes, I step through....
target: 不能停，跑进树林！腿，要有力…… 那里！白浣熊！对，走，带我去！ 大松树旁左转。现在直走，对。熟悉的石头排，对。 冷得胸口痛。身体需要食物。但我得跑回那个……事情发生的地方……第一次看见这只白浣熊的地方！ 两个太阳后，丑女人解开我的手，端着一碗热糊坐下。味道很好，像妈妈用根煮鹿肉汤。肚子想吃。可是丑女人伤害我。我记得疼痛，记得饥饿，决定她是骗子。 她在碗旁放两个小工具。一个我认得，是汤匙，用奇怪银亮的东西做的。另一个，她指着叫它「叉——子」。我看见它尖尖的。我低着眼，慢慢伸手拿叉——子，再慢慢拿碗。 泼！热糊泼上她的脸！接着，把叉——子的尖端刺进她头侧。 她像狼一样嚎叫！我从她颈上扯回宝石，跑！ 她抽人的藤条，把腿打破了。受伤的脚又烫又痛…… 腿，要有力……白浣熊，谢谢你…… 那里，对，倒下的树……那里，脚牙齿夹住我的地方……对…… 这里！ 我像之前一样，把绳子拿在手里，宝石绕着头转，然后，对，我跨了过去……

source:
Two-legged animals. Humans. Won’t leave. Bothering our pasture. More and more. My sibling blades and I – confused. Cannot predict their behavior. We hate their earth-scooping tools. Many cousin blades across the way. Ripped from homes. Tossed here and there. 

Grazers are gone now. Used to come and go. A family of deer. A herd of Buffalo. A gang of elk. A nest of rabbits. They chewed our tips and left. If we were lucky, they left delicious droppings. Ah – to absorb a fresh buffalo dung. Just one more time! 

Humans fenced the area. We are trapped. They return to dig wide holes. They lower their dead into them. Slabs of stone or crossed wood. A mark for each carcass. They jibber jabber. They cry. They leave. They come back to do it again. 

My younger brothers and sisters have weaker roots. Young and trying to grow. It hurts to think of them. I stopped sharing stories of the past. Stories of peace and plenty. It feels unfair. 

Jokes are more kind. 

The snows will cover us soon. A time for thinking. Time to think of jokes. I hope they are clever.  

How can you tell a grass is scared? 

It soils itself.
target:
两脚动物。人类。不肯走。打扰我们的草地。越来越多。我和草叶兄弟姊妹，困惑不解。猜不透他们。我们讨厌他们挖土的工具。对面好多草叶亲戚，被拔离家园，丢得到处都是。

吃草的动物不见了。以前来来去去。一家鹿，一群野牛，一群麋鹿，一窝兔子。啃啃我们的尖端，就离开。运气好，还留下美味的粪便。啊，吸收一坨新鲜牛粪。真想再来一次！

人类围起这块地，我们被困住。他们回来挖大洞，把死人放进去。石板，或交叉的木头，每具尸体一个记号。他们叽哩呱啦，哭泣，离开。再回来，重做一遍。

年幼的弟妹根比较弱，还小，正努力长大。想到他们就难受。我不再讲从前的故事，不再讲和平丰饶的日子。那感觉很不公平。

笑话比较仁慈。

雪很快会覆盖我们。适合思考，适合想笑话。希望想得出聪明的。

怎么知道一棵草吓坏了？

因为它吓得「土」出来。

source: Buffalo Grass: My siblings. This swath of grass family. We proudly survived many winter snows. Many dry summers. We were here first. We refuse intruders. We refuse competition for water and sun. We refuse you!
target: 野牛草：我的兄弟姊妹，这一整片草家族，骄傲地熬过许多冬雪，许多干旱的夏天。我们先来的。不容闯入者，不容争抢水和阳光。不容你！

source: Buffalo Grass: What is this? Hey, hey! My roots feel you down there. Whatever weed you are. Don’t bother sprouting. My family grows wide and thick. We cover this earth. We will choke you out.
target: 野牛草：这是什么？嘿，嘿！我的根感觉到你在下面。不管你是什么杂草，都别发芽。我们家长得又广又密，覆盖这片土地，会把你闷死。

source: “Good news, Corporal. Good news” … Oh, cock and pie! Spare me. Major Ainsworth visits my chamber and goes on about all the good fortune befallen me. My commendation for valor. My recommendation to rank of Captain. All because I managed to crawl back to camp with my scalp on my head while my brothers in red were butchered and given the Indian shave. How can I cry roast meat when I’ll never run again? I – me – a gimp! The entire mission was simply doomed from the start. The previous two scouting parties had been ambushed by the damned Cherokee, why should ours be bloody different? Though, I do recall… seeing a man. A white man donned in animal-skin. Scarred cheek. Fighting most ferociously. Indeed, I remember – I stabbed through a savage with my bayonet and then this strange man whooped and blasted me in the calf with a Queen Anne flintlock pistol, bashed my head with its butt end. I hit the cold earth, stunned. I could only watch. During the rage of battle, before my eyes closed, this strange white man knelt and held the fallen savage by his head, spoke to him desperately, and pressed his lips deeply to the savage’s own. T’was this last image, a disgust branded into my memory, that is perhaps the greatest wound…
target: 「好消息，下士。好消息。」……噢，去他的！饶了我吧。 安斯沃思少校来到病房，滔滔不绝地说我有多走运。英勇嘉奖，推荐晋升上尉。全因我成功爬回营地，头皮还在头上，我的红衣弟兄们却遭屠戮，挨了印第安人的剃刀。 我再也不能跑了，还能有什么好得意？我——堂堂的我——成了瘸子！整趟任务从一开始就注定失败。前两支侦察队都遭该死的切罗基人伏击，我们凭什么会不一样？ 不过，我确实记得……看见一个男人。白人，穿着兽皮，脸颊有疤，作战极其凶猛。对，我想起来了——我用刺刀刺穿一个野人，接着这怪人吼了一声，用安妮女王式燧发手枪打中我的小腿，再用枪托砸我的头。 我倒在冰冷土地上，昏昏沉沉，只能看着。战斗狂乱之中，在我闭眼前，那个奇怪的白人跪下，捧住倒下野人的头，焦急地对他说话，然后将嘴唇深深吻上那野人的嘴。 最后这幕烙印在记忆里的恶心景象，或许才是最深的伤……

source: Nathaniel Asbury: I am… most honored. I… uyo ayelvdi, Chief Great Bear, I cannot. My heart is held by someone else.
target: 纳撒尼尔・阿斯伯里：我……深感荣幸。我……uyo ayelvdi，大熊首领，我不能。我的心已属于别人。

source: Chief Kuwah'hi: Ka! Spring Frog, sit! If you leave me now, you dishonor my invitation, my daughter. You may never return to this…

source: Chief Kuwah'hi: Nathaniel, today you are born among the Cherokee. Today you are named Dustu – Spring Frog. You honor my son, you honor my family, and you honor my people. Are you prepared to receive our people’s mark?

source: Nathaniel Asbury: Wado, Chief Great Bear. I am blessed and grateful – otsaliheliga. Your eldest son, Akikta – Determined One, helped me many springs ago to escape Shawnee braves who murdered my family. This cheek scar… it is my constant reminder of his bravery. That debt is mine until my spirit becomes formless to join Unetlanvhi.
target: 纳撒尼尔・阿斯伯里：Wado，大熊首领。我蒙受祝福，心怀感激——otsaliheliga。许多个春天前，您的长子Akikta，坚定者，帮我逃离杀害我家人的肖尼战士。这道脸颊疤痕……时时提醒我他的英勇。这份恩情，我会记到灵魂无形、与Unetlanvhi合一之时。

source: Chief Kuwah'hi: You speak of debts? You have taught many of us to speak in the white man’s tongue. You taught Gawanii to read their written code. You saved Akikta from the red-cloth tsosdidanuwi two suns ago. His stomach wound heals. The debt is mine, Spring Frog. So I proudly ask that you take my daughter in spiritual union.
target: 库瓦希首领：你说恩情？你教我们许多人说白人的语言，教加瓦尼读懂他们的文字。两个太阳前，你从红衣tsosdidanuwi手中救下阿基克塔，他腹部的伤正在愈合。欠情的是我，春蛙。因此，我骄傲地请你与我的女儿结为灵魂伴侣。

source: Chief Kuwah'hi: Spring Frog! Fool!
target: 库瓦希首领：春蛙！蠢材！

source: Chief Kuwah'hi: Ah. It is, then, as I fear. Do not think it is not seen. You and Akikta. You have lain together. It is asegi… not the tradition. You know this. A man must be a man. He has given his word to take Tsiyi for a wife and he will bear many strong Tsalagi…
target: 库瓦希首领：啊，果然如我所惧。别以为没人看见。你和阿基克塔，你们同床共枕了。那是asegi……不合传统。你知道的。男人就该是男人。他已承诺娶齐伊，会生下许多强壮的Tsalagi……
